# Vertical cell alignment of page and column anchors

Original OPC/XML controls generated by tools/mixed_cell_alignment_fixture.py
from this repository's independent mixed-cell-anchor package. Twelve pages
cross horizontal page/column coordinates, a blue picture/zero-height line, and
cell top/center/bottom alignment. Every anchor uses a numeric page-relative
vertical offset, wrapNone and layoutInCell=true in compatibility mode 15.
Rows have an exact 80pt height and anchor cells have a 12pt left margin.
Column-relative anchors include that margin; page-relative anchors do not.
Arial is explicit so native and browser text
metrics use the same face; the initial implicit-font diagnostic was superseded.

The reference application exported the retained PDF from the final source opened read-only.
Native blue raster bounds at 96 DPI are in reference.json. All twelve pages
were visually inspected. hashes.json binds source, PDF and page PNGs.

The reference application includes the drawing's bottom in the content extent for vertical cell
alignment, then translates both text and drawing by the resulting shift. The
picture therefore leaves less free space than the flat line. This is distinct
from wp:positionV/wp:align, which the earlier page/margin controls establish is
ignored for these cell-bound anchors. wrapNone does not resize the exact row.
ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.85 (vAlign), 20.4.2.3 (layoutInCell), 20.4.2.10–13
(positions) apply. No additional reference/spec divergence is claimed by this control.

Browser coverage compares every native blue mask in both directions within one
pixel and repeats after editing/export/reopening. Unit coverage checks content
shifts, fixed row height, retained coordinate XML, edit/reimport and exact undo.
